title: eval-harness: add per-prompt regression CI hook and metrics integration
author: Asha Patel
description: Adds a per-prompt regression CI hook to the eval-harness pipeline and integrates prompt-level metrics into CI reports. Motivation: customers see regressions that affect small but important prompt subsets; global quality gates miss these. This change introduces a lightweight hook that runs a per-prompt delta check against a pinned baseline, exports per-prompt metrics (accuracy/coverage/semantic-similarity), and wires those metrics into existing CI annotations and the GitHub check output. The change includes a configurable thresholds file (eval/ci/prompt_gates.yaml) with sensible defaults, an opt-in Linear-based mapping to link failing prompt groups to Linear tickets, and a small migration to add deterministic ordering for eval examples to reduce test flakiness. The PR is conservative: feature is opt-in via repo config (eval.ci.enable_per_prompt_gates = true) and defaults to non-blocking for repositories without a baseline. Includes unit tests, an end-to-end smoke check that runs in CI with a sampled prompt set, and docs updates describing how to tune gates and interpret reports. Related Linear: ENG-4219, ENG-4280. Related support ticket: SUP-1023.
commits: feat(eval-harness): add per-prompt gating hook and reporting
test(eval-harness): add unit tests for prompt delta computation and thresholding
ci: wire metrics exporter to GitHub checks and add annotations
fix(test): deterministic ordering for sampled prompts to reduce flakiness
docs: add section describing per-prompt gates and tuning guidance
ci_checks_summary: Initial CI run showed a flaky test in eval-harness e2e due to nondeterministic prompt sampling; fixed by adding deterministic seed and explicit ordering. Re-run: build: pass, unit-tests: pass, eval-harness-e2e (sampled): pass, lint: pass. Metrics exporter annotations attached to GitHub check with per-prompt deltas and links to detailed S3 artifact.
review_comments: Ravi Singh: This looks great overall. Two asks: (1) make the default gating non-blocking for repos without a saved baseline, and (2) can we add a small backstop to avoid noisy false-positives when sample size is tiny?
Asha Patel: Thanks Ravi — both addressed. The gate is opt-in and non-blocking by default; added a min_sample_size check and fallback to a warning annotation when sample size < 30.

Lena Cho: Noted the deterministic ordering change — can you call that out in the PR body/docs so teams know historical diffs may change? Also suggest a short migration note for customers with custom baselines.
Asha Patel: Added docs section and migration notes. Also included a smoke e2e job that runs the gate in non-blocking mode to preview results before teams opt-in to blocking enforcement.
Connor McBride: CI annotations look useful. One nit: prefer the metric name 'prompt_semantic_similarity' to 'prompt_similarity' for clarity.
release_notes: Add opt-in per-prompt regression gating for eval-harness with CI integration and per-prompt metric exports. Defaults to non-blocking; configurable thresholds and min-sample sizing. See docs/eval-harness/per-prompt-gating.md for usage and tuning.
